scope: Self-contained concept tutorial with discussion cues. No audience software steps.

slides.title: Agentic AI: Three Operator Cases
slides.say: Understand the problem, follow the agent and review the evidence. 90 minutes / three what-if discussions The examples are self-contained. No computer or software setup is needed. We will follow a goal, the agent’s requests, numerical evidence and a human decision. The results come from reduced or synthetic studies; they are examples for learning.

slides.title: An agent chooses what to try next
slides.say: Give the agent a goal. It requests a tool, reads the result and chooses the next step. The agent does not calculate the electrical result by writing a confident answer. It chooses a permitted tool, reads the result and decides whether another request or human review is needed. Trace the feedback arrow once with the audience.

slides.title: The agent asks; the tool calculates
slides.say: A tool does one job. An agent can connect several jobs using their results. The Stanford figure distinguishes one function call from a longer agentic workflow. A function can perform one calculation. An agentic workflow connects requests and uses returned results to decide what comes next.

slides.title: Solar settings: which option should we try?
slides.say: Compare possible settings, then check voltage and line current. The agent can organize these trials and report the checked options. Suppose an operator needs new solar settings. Different settings affect voltage, current and useful solar output. The agent organizes a bounded study; the numerical tool supplies the engineering evidence.

slides.title: Give the agent a goal and clear limits
slides.say: State the goal, allowed tools and stopping rules. Keep the operator’s review step explicit. A useful request states the operating goal, available tools and stopping conditions. The agent needs to know when it must ask for review rather than continue trying options. The operator defines these boundaries.

slides.title: Restoration: who should get power first?
slides.say: The operator sets the service priority. That priority changes the study the agent requests. When supply is limited, restoring the greatest total power can differ from protecting essential services. The operator chooses that priority. The agent must preserve it when requesting and comparing studies.

slides.title: Keep three jobs clear
slides.say: The agent requests a study. The tool calculates. The operator reviews the result. Keep the jobs separate. The agent coordinates requests. The numerical tool calculates. The operator reviews the evidence and decides the next authorized step. A tool passing its checks is not operating permission.

slides.title: Wrong readings can still fit a model
slides.say: A good fit alone does not prove that the readings are true. The agent can organize checks and flag missing evidence. Readings may fit a model and still be wrong. An alarm test measures one kind of mismatch. The agent can request additional checks and identify missing information, but its explanation cannot make a data source trustworthy.

slides.title: Case 1: which solar settings should we use?
slides.say: Choose settings that keep voltage and line current within the allowed range. An agent can organize the trials and return checked options. Start with the physical problem: choose solar controls that respect voltage, current and equipment capacity while serving the stated generation goal. The agent can organize trials and return a checked option. It does not replace the solver or the operator.

slides.title: Two tools suggest different settings
slides.say: MPC plans with a model. SAC uses a previously trained controller. Treat both outputs as proposals that need the same electrical checks. MPC means model predictive control: it plans with a model. SAC means soft actor-critic: it uses a previously trained policy. Both produce proposals. Apply the same electrical checks to each before comparing cost or usefulness.

Use the tool to calculate those effects rather than infer safety from the control names.

slides.say: A fault removes a supply path. Available capacity limits what can be restored. The operator sets priorities; the agent can request and check restoration options. A fault removes one supply path in the six-node network. The available backup capacity limits which loads can be restored. Cyan marks the critical loads. The operator defines priorities, while the agent can request alternative restoration studies.

slides.title: How the agent helps restore service
slides.say: Choose the goal: critical loads first, or the most total power. The agent can request a study, read the trade-off and ask for a new study when limits change. The goal changes the requested optimization. The agent should keep the operator’s priority, ask the tool for a plan, read service and capacity checks, and request a new study when inputs change. The solver decides which whole loads fit the network constraints.

slides.title: The service goal changes the study request
slides.say: Critical-first gives more weight to essential service. Most-total-power aims to restore the largest amount of power. Critical-first assigns more value to essential service. Most-total-power maximizes total restored kW. Both still need the same network constraints. The agent translates the selected goal into the appropriate permitted study request; the solver performs the optimization.

At a 40 kW backup tie, the critical-first result restores 130 kW total, including 90 kW critical. The total-power result restores 140 kW, including only 30 kW critical. Neither objective removes the need to explain the service trade-off. In the plots, overlapping markers indicate equal outcomes.

slides.say: One wrong reading may conflict with the other readings. Coordinated changes may still look consistent with the model. One biased reading can disagree with the remaining data. slides.title: Multi-agent framework used in these cases
slides.say: The five roles share the same case facts and checked results. One Llama model handles planning and refinement. Python calculates and checks. Awareness reads the shared case. Planning prepares permitted options and uses Llama to choose a study. Simulation calculates. Verification checks limits and case identity. The Llama optimizer requests a bounded change or ranks passing options. Every changed trial returns for simulation and verification. Python guards the final choice before operator review. One Llama model fills two roles; this is not five independent language models. The implementation uses case-specific numerical tools behind the same stages.

slides.question: Which roles use Llama, and who checks a revised proposal?
slides.answer: Planning and the optimizer use one Llama model. Python performs fresh simulation, verification and a final guarded check before operator review.

slides.title: Explain one case in your own words
slides.say: What is the operator’s problem, and what should the agent request next? Which tool result supports the proposal, and what must the operator still decide? Ask participants to choose one case and explain the complete loop in their own words. They should name the problem, an agent request, a returned numerical fact and a remaining human decision. Optional practice materials can be used after the concept tutorial, but no account or code is needed for this discussion.
